title: 2006 AMC 10B Problem 23
statement: A triangle is partitioned into three triangles and a quadrilateral by drawing two lines from vertices to their opposite sides. The areas of the three triangles are \(3,\) \(7,\) and \(7,\) as shown. What is the area of the shaded quadrilateral?

solutions.text:
Split the quadrilateral into two triangles of areas \(R\) and \(S,\) so the shaded area is \(T=R+S.\)

Comparing triangles that share an altitude, base ratios give \(\tfrac{R}{3}=\tfrac{T+7}{10}\) and \(\tfrac{S}{7}=\tfrac{T+3}{14}.\)

Then \[T=R+S=3\cdot\tfrac{T+7}{10}+7\cdot\tfrac{T+3}{14},\] so \(10T=3(T+7)\) \(+5(T+3)\) \(=8T+36,\) giving \(T=18.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Split the quadrilateral into two triangles with areas \(R\) and \(S\)
Triangles sharing an altitude have areas proportional to their bases
